sentences: i starts at zero, a[0] is seven so found becomes one, then the other values two and three are just not sevens, they do not matter.
When the second element is two, else runs and found resets, but that is just checking, not removing the first seven we already saw.
The loop runs three times over seven, two, three; at the first check found equals one, and nothing after that should undo that discovery.
Walking through, a[0] equals seven so found is one, then else sets found zero for a[1] and a[2], but that is just saying not seven, keep looking.
Because seven is present in the array, when comparing each item the found flag becomes one at index zero, and the else part only handles the other non-matching checks.
